001package io.jstach.rainbowgum.format;
002
003import io.jstach.rainbowgum.annotation.CaseChanging;
004import io.jstach.rainbowgum.annotation.EnumAlias;
005
006/**
007 * How the core <code>json5</code> encoder lays out each event's object. Only whitespace
008 * outside values is added, so the output parses the same. Ignored for plain JSON.
009 */
010@CaseChanging
011public enum Json5PrettyPrint {
012
013        /**
014         * No added whitespace: <code>level:"INFO",logger:...</code>.
015         */
016        @EnumAlias("false")
017        OFF,
018        /**
019         * Pads after the level's closing quote so the fields after it line up:
020         * <code>level:"INFO" ,logger:...</code>. The default.
021         */
022        @EnumAlias("default")
023        LEVEL_PADDING,
024        /**
025         * Level padding and a space after every comma:
026         * <code>level:"INFO" , logger:"com.example.App", threadId:...</code>.
027         */
028        SPACING,
029        /**
030         * Each of the event's fields on its own line, indented one space like the
031         * <code>rainbowgum-json</code> encoders' pretty print, with nested key values on one
032         * line. The level is not padded.
033         */
034        @EnumAlias("true")
035        FULL;
036
037        static Json5PrettyPrint parse(String value) {
038                return switch (value.strip().toLowerCase(java.util.Locale.ROOT)) {
039                        case "default" -> LEVEL_PADDING;
040                        case "true" -> FULL;
041                        case "false" -> OFF;
042                        default ->
043                                io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogProperty.enumValue(Json5PrettyPrint.class, value, "true", "false", "default");
044                };
045        }
046
047}
